Last Friday (the 21st), in the ruling of the Hong Kong Alliance case, during the early morning hours, police took a woman who was queuing to observe the hearing into a police vehicle. The police replied to inquiries stating that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent."

Last Friday at around 5 a.m., more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During this time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue "suspected her clothing might have a bit of seditious intent" and took her away in a police vehicle. While officers were taking the woman away, several officers kept instructing journalists to leave, saying "take you to the press area," and extended the orange cordon line towards the direction of Ying Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, they withdrew the cordon line. On that day, a "court observer" who was queuing near the woman pointed out that she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

《集誌社》 inquired with the police about the reasons for the woman being taken away and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation in the West Kowloon court area on August 21, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent," and was detained for investigation.
